articles.title: Tamil Nadu: Supreme Court upholds FIR order against DMK leader KN Nehru in Rs 634-crore cash-for-jobs scam
articles.description: The Supreme Court’s decision to uphold the Madras High Court’s direction to register an FIR against former DMK minister KN Nehru in the alleged Rs 634-crore cash-for-jobs scam, along with two other legal setbacks involving DMK leaders, has intensified scrutiny of corruption allegations against the party’s senior functionaries in Tamil Nadu. Supreme Court upholds FIR direction against KN Nehru Dismissing a petition filed by former DMK minister KN Nehru on November 2, the Supreme Court bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said there was no ground to interfere with the Madras High Court’s February 20 judgment and October 26 order. On October 26, the High Court dismissed Nehru’s review petition challenging its earlier order, which directed the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to register a case based on information provided by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) regarding the alleged Rs 634-crore cash-for-jobs scam. It refused to reconsider its February 20 order directing the DVAC to register an FIR. While refusing to entertain Nehru’s plea or pass any order in his favour, the Supreme Court said the High Court’s direction to register an FIR did not warrant interference under Article 136 of the Constitution. The apex court’s decision will enable the DVAC to register an FIR and probe allegations of a multi-crore scam involving the senior DMK leader. The bench observed that a thorough investigation was necessary, as Nehru was heading the ministry under scrutiny over alleged recruitment irregularities. The bench also said Nehru was entitled to raise all points in his defence, in accordance with law, during future proceedings before the court. It may be recalled that the ED had come across incriminating material in April 2025 while conducting a search and seizure operation in connection with a bank fraud case at the premises of Nehru’s brother, N Ravichandran. It subsequently shared the information with the Tamil Nadu DGP under Section 66 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002. The data shared by the ED disclosed that crores of rupees had allegedly changed hands through hawala transactions for filling 2,538 posts of Assistant Engineer, Junior Engineer and Town Planning Officer in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department. Also Read: Tamil Nadu: Anti-Corruption wing books senior DMK leader KN Nehru, associates over Rs 1,020 crore tender irregularities The material reportedly revealed the receipt of bribes ranging from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 35 lakh per candidate and the sharing of call letters with candidates even before they were officially selected and appointed. Nehru had challenged the direction before the Supreme Court, arguing that the ED’s information was unverified and could not form the basis of an FIR. He also contended that the High Court had erred in directing the DVAC to register a case against him without conducting a preliminary inquiry. The apex court, however, rejected his contentions, found no merit in the plea and refused to interfere with the High Court’s order. Former DMK minister Anbil Mahesh gets police custody In another development, a special court dealing with cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act on November 2 granted police custody of former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi until November 4. Anbil Mahesh was arrested on October 26 by the Chennai Central Crime Branch (CCB) in connection with an alleged Rs 100-crore scam. The case was registered following a complaint by D.C. Elangovan, secretary of the Federation of Associations of Private Schools in Tamil Nadu. He alleged that money was collected from school managements on the promise of securing government approvals, including permanent recognition, school upgradation, Directorate of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) clearances and other statutory permissions. Supreme Court rejects Akash Baskaran’s plea in TASMAC probe In yet another development on November 2, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed film producer Akash Baskaran’s plea challenging the Madras High Court’s decision to close his petition questioning ED searches linked to the TASMAC money-laundering probe. The Supreme Court dismisses film producer Akash Baskaran’s plea against the Madras High Court closing his petition challenging ED searches linked to the TASMAC money-laundering probe.#SupremeCourt pic.twitter.com/HNoa2tOx4q — LawChakra (@LawChakra) November 2, 2026 The CJI Surya Kant-led bench observed that the seized articles had already been returned and the show-cause notice withdrawn. The bench noted that any fresh proceedings would require the adjudicating authority to apply its mind afresh. Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra argued that the High Court ought to have adjudicated the legality of the searches instead of relegating Baskaran to the appellate forum, particularly when there was no adjudication order against him. Also Read: Tamil Nadu: DVAC raids 30 locations linked to former DMK minister KN Nehru, seizes 241 documents The bench, however, declined to interfere, observing that the High Court’s findings concerning the search were made at the interim stage and that questions relating to any future attachment proceedings would have to be considered separately. Akash Baskaran, owner of Dawn Pictures, is currently embroiled in legal scrutiny surrounding a high-profile Rs 1,000-crore PMLA probe related to alleged irregularities in the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC). In June this year, a Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan of the Madras High Court closed a writ petition filed by Akash Baskaran challenging the search proceedings initiated by the ED in connection with the alleged money-laundering investigation linked to TASMAC. The court, however, granted him liberty to raise all objections before the Appellate Tribunal under the PMLA. The court observed that an identical challenge arising from the same search proceedings had already been disposed of by relegating the petitioner therein to pursue remedies before the appellate forum after the attachment proceedings had been confirmed by the Adjudicating Authority. The latest Supreme Court setback adds to the mounting corruption allegations surrounding senior DMK leader and former minister KN Nehru, a close associate of former Chief Minister MK Stalin. articles.title: ISA Report Makes Case For Achieving 888 GWh of Energy Storage by 2035–36 In India
articles.description: India will require 888 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2035–36 to support its expanding renewable energy base and maintain grid reliability, according to the report India’s Energy Storage by the International Solar Alliance (ISA). The report identifies project execution, financing, market development, domestic manufacturing and regulatory coordination as key factors that will determine whether the country can meet its growing storage requirements. The Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) projections indicate that the requirement comprises 321 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and 567 GWh of Pumped Storage Projects (PSP). The report also outlines a requirement of 2,380 GWh by 2047 under its stated scenario, in line with the country’s broader Viksit Bharat 2047 ambitions. The report highlights that while India has made progress in establishing a policy framework for energy storage, the next phase will depend on converting procurement activity into commissioned projects and creating a commercially sustainable ecosystem. It calls for coordinated action across planning, regulation, investment, grid integration and manufacturing to accelerate deployment. Execution and Market Reforms Key to Scaling Storage A key concern highlighted in the report is the gap between energy storage tenders and their conversion into operational assets. Although India has pursued tenders for Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE), solar projects combined with BESS, and standalone battery storage, the conversion of awarded capacity into Power Sale Agreements has remained a challenge. The report recommends moving beyond single application procurement models focused primarily on energy arbitrage. Future tender structures, it says, should incorporate multiple revenue streams, capacity support provisions and stronger enforcement mechanisms for Power Sale Agreements. It also calls for the development of market mechanisms that allow storage assets to participate in ancillary services and other grid support functions. Revenue stacking, which enables storage projects to earn from multiple applications, is identified as an important step towards reducing dependence on government support and improving project viability. Three Scenarios Map India's Storage Deployment Path The report presents three possible deployment scenarios: Policy as Stated, Accelerated and Constrained. These account for differences in policy implementation, investment, technology adoption, manufacturing growth and project execution. Under the Policy as Stated scenario, India's storage requirement is projected at 888 GWh by 2035–36 and 2,380 GWh by 2047. The Accelerated scenario estimates that capacity could reach 1,000–1,150 GWh by 2035–36 and 3,000–3,500 GWh by 2047, supported by faster project execution, stronger investment, revenue stacking and domestic manufacturing. The report clarifies that these are scenario based estimates rather than official targets. It also notes that a definitive 2070 storage projection would require further modelling, given the uncertainty surrounding future technology costs, policy continuity and global supply chains. Report Sets Out Phased Actions Through 2070 The report's recommendations are organised across immediate, near term, medium term and long term priorities. Actions proposed by 2027 include strengthening certification and enforcement, resolving classification related ambiguity for containerised BESS, mandating grid forming inverters in new BESS tenders and completing the allocation of the second tranche of Viability Gap Funding. For 2027 to 2030, the focus shifts to enabling revenue stacking, opening ancillary services to storage, reforming Energy Storage Obligations through state specific targets and establishing a regulatory framework for behind the meter storage. The report also recommends setting up a National Energy Storage Testing Centre. Between 2030 and 2035, the proposed priorities include transitioning towards market driven procurement and achieving more than 40 per cent domestic value addition in BESS. Longer term recommendations extend to strengthening India's domestic value chain, expanding battery recycling and positioning the country as a supplier of energy storage technologies and expertise.

articles.title: Daily News Wrap-Up: Solar Tendering Surges 61% in Q3 2026
articles.description: Government agencies stepped up solar tendering activity in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, reversing the previous quarter’s slowdown. Tendering increased 61% quarter-over-quarter, while auction activity declined 10%.

articles.title: TN floats tenders for breakfast scheme supplies as beneficiary count crosses 34 lakh
articles.description: Chennai, Nov 4 (IANS) The Tamil Nadu government has invited nationwide electronic tenders for the procurement of food ingredients required for the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme, which currently benefits more than 34 lakh children studying in government and government-aided schools across the state. The procurement, to be undertaken through the state's consumer cooperative network, is intended to ensure uninterrupted implementation of the breakfast programme during the three-month period beginning January 1, 2027. According to the tender notification, the government proposes to procure 1,300 metric tonnes of double-roasted rava in one-kilogram packets and 1,200 metric tonnes of samba rava, also packed in one-kilogram quantities, along with another category of food ingredients supplied in 200-gram packets. The tender documents became available for downloading on November 2, while December 2 has been fixed as the deadline for submitting bids. Suppliers from across India can participate in the electronic tendering process. Custom Ad: Multiplex The breakfast initiative has its origins in the Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme launched on September 15, 2022, by the then DMK government headed by M.K. Stalin. The programme was introduced to provide nutritious morning meals to primary schoolchildren, particularly those from economically disadvantaged families. Initially implemented in selected schools, the scheme was subsequently expanded in phases to cover government primary schools across Tamil Nadu. Its coverage was later extended to government-aided institutions, substantially increasing the number of beneficiaries. In September, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay expanded the programme to students in Classes 6 to 8, bringing approximately 34.64 lakh children in 44,984 schools under its coverage. The expansion required an additional allocation of Rs 217.63 crore, taking the programme's overall allocation to Rs 724 crore. The scheme provides freshly prepared breakfast, including pongal, upma, kichadi and other nutritious dishes, before regular classroom activities begin. Its principal objectives are to prevent classroom hunger, improve nutritional standards, encourage school attendance and help children concentrate on their studies. An evaluation by the State Planning Commission found improved attendance in 1,319 of the 1,543 schools surveyed, indicating encouraging results from the initiative. The latest procurement exercise also includes 1,300 metric tonnes of semiya, or vermicelli, in 200-gram packets, completing the three categories of ingredients covered by the tender process. --IANS aal/dpb

articles.title: Maha audit flags irregularities in ₹37.61-crore malaria spending; Abitkar vows action
articles.description: The audit report points to lapses in tendering, including failure to constitute purchase committees, publish newspaper advertisements and use the Centre’s Government e-Marketplace portal. It also alleges that preferred suppliers were awarded contracts.
